value: Solving "too large to make" through large-format printing.
Large-format additive manufacturing (WAAM/LFAM) is going commercial in Europe. We connect large-scale metal and polymer 3D printing to real problems on Japan's factory floor.

Turnkey systems with build volumes from 2x1m to 3x2m are now commercially available replacing work once written off as "too small a lot to tool up for" or "too large to machine." No tooling means the economics work from a single unit.
Where it is already ahead overseas
Overseas cases are based on manufacturer-published materials and do not represent our own track record.
The common thread -- one-off large high-mix -- is exactly what conventional processes handle worst.

Entry-level turnkey systems run roughly EUR400000-450000 with a standard lead time of 18-24 weeks after firm order (manufacturer-provided figures). Japan's labor-saving investment subsidy catalog has included 3D printers since October 2025 adding tailwind to the investment case. At this scale of investment careful screening before ordering has real value.
We judge fit before you commit

We screen against four conditions -- part size lot volume material and current process cost/lead time -- to judge whether large-format printing will actually help. Telling you it is not a fit when it is not is part of the job.

We are not an exclusive agent for any single manufacturer. We work non-exclusively case by case to bridge you to European manufacturers -- building a project brief from your requirements and connecting you directly with the manufacturer's team designed alongside Japan's existing machining grinding heat-treatment and inspection network.
